subject: Cost-latency decomposition: sprint owners & minimal telemetry asks
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Claire Moss <claire@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cost-latency decomposition: sprint owners & minimal telemetry asks

Team / Claire —

Quick ask to align scope for next sprint: ACME has asked for a per-route cost + latency "decomposition" tile in the Console (they want to see per-endpoint median / 95th latency and cost per 1k tokens, with a simple sort/filter by tenant). Before I scope engineering work I need:

- a compact owner matrix (who owns ingest, agg, UI surface, and rollout)
- a minimal telemetry column set we can commit to (fields + retention)
- any security/compliance constraints that would affect sampling or retention for ACME

I attached a sketch (decomp-proposal-v1.pdf) that maps a naive pipeline. Can each of you reply with the owner you recommend and one-line blockers by EOD tomorrow?

Goal: get a sprint-ready ticket set and acceptance criteria by Mon so we can include this in the July 26 sprint planning.

Thanks —
Ben
Product Partnerships (Sales Eng)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: decomp-proposal-v1.pdf

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Claire Moss <claire@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost-latency decomposition: sprint owners & minimal telemetry asks

Ben —

Agree this is MVP-friendly. My suggested owner mapping (quick):

- Data ingest & sampling: Marissa Cole (owns ingest pipeline and prefix/KV cache tagging)
- Aggregation / metrics schema: Diego Fernandez (aggregation, rollups, 95th computation)
- Console UI + UX: Kimberly Park (tile design, drill modal, sorting)
- PM / rollout coordination: Ben Carter (evangelize and acceptance with ACME)

Minimal telemetry column set (proposal):
- timestamp, tenant_id, route_id, request_tokens, response_tokens, latency_ms, error_flag, model_variant, region
- retention: raw events 7d, 1h rollups 90d, 1d rollups 540d
\Blockers / risks (one-liners):
- Marissa: sampling needs to guarantee unbiased 95th — we need to confirm where sample is taken (client vs runtime).
- Diego: 95th on small slices may be noisy; need a min sample threshold or fallback to percentile-estimate.
- Kimberly: tile needs pre-aggregates; producing them on-demand will blow query cost unless we cap route cardinality.

Attaching a draft owner matrix (owners-matrix.xlsx). I'm happy to host a 30-min sync tomorrow if folks prefer to converge live.

—Lauren
Director, Observability Product
Redwood Inference

Attachments: owners-matrix.xlsx

From: Claire Moss <claire@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jul 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost-latency decomposition: sprint owners & minimal telemetry asks

Thanks Ben / Lauren —

ACME priorities (short):
1) We need per-route 95th and median latency (for production routes) exposed to product owners.
2) Cost estimate: cost per 1k tokens for each route (preferably broken down by model variant).
3) Sampling guarantee: if you sample, provide lower-bound confidence for percentiles or a flag that sample < X.

Constraints from our side: certain PII-containing routes must be marked and excluded from cross-tenant rollups; we can share a list. Also, we have a single-region data residency requirement for these metrics (US-east) — will that break any of your ingestion assumptions?

If you can provide a minimal JSON schema for the telemetry and a target acceptance criteria (e.g., sample floor, retention windows, expected query latency for the tile), we can mark this priority and fast-track an internal sign-off.

—Claire Moss
Platform Product Lead, ACME Inc.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Claire Moss <claire@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost-latency decomposition: sprint owners & minimal telemetry asks

Thanks — good alignment. Summary / next steps (agreed):

1) Owners (confirmed): Marissa = ingest/sampling; Diego = aggregation/percentiles; Kimberly = UI/acceptance; Ben = PM/sign-off with ACME.
2) Minimal telemetry schema: Lauren's proposed column set is approved as the MVP. Marissa: please produce a small JSON schema by Monday that includes the PII-exclusion flag and region tag (us-east).
3) Sampling policy: Marissa and Diego will propose a sample-floor policy (min 100 samples per route per hour) or an explicit "confidence" flag added to results. Diego: include fallback behavior for small-sample slices.
4) Rollout & acceptance: Build sprint tickets for July 26 sprint (INFR-1123). Acceptance criteria: tile shows median & 95th for top 50 routes, cost per 1k tokens by model variant, and a clear "insufficient sample" indicator.
5) Meeting: let's do a 30-min runbook/hand-off on Mon 19 Jul 2027 10:00 PDT — Kimberly, please confirm.

Action items (owners):
- Marissa: JSON schema + sampling proposal (due Mon 19 Jul)
- Diego: aggregation implementation notes + estimator for small samples (due Tue 20 Jul)
- Kimberly: wireframe and drill acceptance criteria (due Tue 20 Jul)
- Ben: create Jira epic + ACME acceptance checklist (INFR-1123)

I attached a short acceptance draft (sprint-1-acceptance.md). Please add any changes directly to the Drive link and I'll convert to tickets early next week.

Ben
Product Partnerships (Sales Eng)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sprint-1-acceptance.md
